title: $\mathrm{Ex}_!^c$ is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ for a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]),
or $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]). For every cartesian square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{\;g'\;} & X\\
{\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{\;g\;} & Y
\end{array}
$$
of the setting and every compactification $c$ of $f$, with base-changed compactification $c'$ of
$f'$, the compact-support base change morphism
$$
\mathrm{Ex}_!^c\colon Lg^*\circ Rf_!^c\longrightarrow Rf'^{\,c'}_!\circ Lg'^*
$$
of [det-def-sfb-shriek-base-change-morphism-definition] is an isomorphism of functors
$D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y',\Lambda)$. No properness of $f$ is assumed.

proof.text:
By [det-def-sfb-shriek-base-change-morphism-definition],
$\mathrm{Ex}_!^c=Rp'_*(\mathrm{Ex}^j)^{-1}\circ\mathrm{BC}_{i_!}$. The first factor $\mathrm{BC}_{i_!}$ is a
natural isomorphism by [det-thm-sfb-shriek-base-change-proper-step]; this is the only place where
properness enters, through the proper morphism $p$ of the compactification, not through $f$. The
second factor is $Rp'_*$ applied to the inverse of the extension-by-zero exchange isomorphism of the
cartesian square $(g',i,i',\bar g)$, which is invertible for every commutative condensed ring
([thm-sfb-dc-open-base-change-iso]); a functor carries natural isomorphisms to natural isomorphisms.
A composite of natural isomorphisms is a natural isomorphism.
